<reason>Side A wins by successfully framing the proposition as a normative choice about defaults and burdens of proof, arguing that home care is the ethical baseline institutions must justify overriding. While Side B mounts a vigorous practical challenge regarding labor scarcity and safety risks, its attempt to expose a contradiction in A's position regarding 24/7 care mischaracterizes A's argument—A's "when possible" qualifier allows for need-based flexibility rather than inconsistency. A's closing effectively crystallizes the choice between organizing care around human dignity versus administrative convenience.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 A1, which sharply pressed A on the apparent tension between dismissing 24/7 staffing as a strawman in the Pressure Questions and then promising overnight aides in Rebuttal 2, forcing A to clarify that support levels should match individual needs.</best_rebuttal>
